headline: IMF estimates AI circular financing at a little over $1 trillion
body: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva says the world economy is "standing on one leg" on AI. The IMF estimates circular financing among AI companies at a little over $1 trillion, with two-thirds funded by debt.
note: Two-thirds of it is funded by debt, which makes the AI leg a financing question as well as a market one. Georgieva warned that if this leg wobbles, that can lead to financial stability troubles, while characterizing the recent market swings as "orderly" and urging caution.

figure.label: IMF estimate of AI circular financing, two-thirds funded by debt

evidence.text: The global economy is "on the AI leg," International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said Monday, warning that the overdependence on the sector risks the world's financial stability.
We have a world economy that is standing on one leg on the AI leg.
"If this leg wobbles, that can lead to financial stability troubles," Georgieva warned.

Circular financing among AI companies — where money invested in an AI company ultimately flows back to the investor through purchase orders — has grown to a little over $1 trillion, two-thirds of it funded by debt, the IMF estimates.
Georgieva on Monday characterized the recent market swings as "orderly," and unlikely to spiral into anything that could undermine the world economy, while urging caution.
